work.name: Viterra Robotics, Chengdu, China
highlights: Established an end-to-end sim-to-real development workflow for quadrotor autonomy, spanning simulation, onboard deployment, and real-world flight validation.
Developed autonomous exploration and motion planning algorithms for quadrotors navigating complex, GPS-denied environments.
Conducted flight-dynamics identification and control-oriented modeling, and developed physics-informed learning methods for external force and torque estimation.

work.name: Inspire AG, Zurich, Switzerland
highlights: Developed an assembly motion recognition and real-time error detection system with Bossard AG and Intelliact AG.
Validated the system through field tests at Stäubli and Mettler-Toledo factories.

projects.name: Assembly Motion Generation for Action Recognition
projects.summary: Master's Thesis Student, ETH Zurich. Grade: 6.0/6.0. Advisor: Prof. Dr. Mirko Meboldt (Pd|z).
highlights: Used reinforcement learning with the GraspXL framework for scalable dexterous grasp generation.
Synthesized assembly motions with a grasping hand in simulation.
Trained action recognition models using synthetic assembly motions and labels.

projects.name: Adversarial Learning via Differentiable Simulation
projects.summary: Semester Project Student, ETH Zurich. Advisor: Prof. Fan Shi (ETH AI Center).
highlights: Developed adversarial attacks on quadruped locomotion policies using gradient information from differentiable simulation.
Applied projected gradient descent to joint-state inputs to disrupt legged robot locomotion.

projects.name: Adaptive Mechanism Design in Sequential Social Dilemmas
projects.summary: Student, ETH Zurich. Advisor: Dr. Vinzenz Thoma (D-INFK, ETH AI Center).
highlights: Reimplemented the adaptive mechanism design (AMD) algorithm using Ray RLlib, validated it on the prisoner's dilemma, and adapted it to more complex multi-agent environments.
Provided open-source implementations of the Wolfpack and Gathering environments.

projects.name: Navigation of Mobile Robots on Rough Terrain
projects.summary: Research Assistant, Tsinghua University, Shenzhen, China. Advisor: Prof. Xueqian Wang.
highlights: Developed real-time SLAM and navigation for the AgileX SCOUT platform on extremely rough terrain.
Used model predictive control (MPC) and control barrier functions (CBFs) for local collision avoidance, and PF-RRT* for global planning.
Built point-cloud maps of complex terrain.
